newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end mostly flat in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end mostly flat in range-bound trade.

text.p: ** (1000 GMT) - Shares at the Bombay Stock Exchange close
mixed, but market undertone remains firm
** End-account considerations weigh on market, foreign
funds make small purchases in select stocks
** Bombay's top share index ends 8.02 pts, or 0.21 pct down
** Shares of Thomas Cook end marginally higher after
surging five percent. Company says to meet for bonus
** National Stock Exchange 50-stock index up 3.80 pts, or
Pivotals finished mixed at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, in a session which traders described as "boring" and "uninspiring".
"I think the market will be stuck at these levels or lower to about 3,600," said R. Balakrishnan, president at Bombay-based, Dil Vikas Finance.
Lack of active participation by foreign funds and low retail investments were the major factors blocking the market's climb to higher levels, traders said.
"It's mostly a wait-and-watch policy now," Balakrishnan said.
